title: CSS page transition: four portals between my 17 CV worlds
meta_description: How I swapped a theme dropdown for world cards and four CSS portal effects, timed by a small state machine and picked from a shuffle bag.
audience: software engineers who build front ends
promise: A CSS page transition that covers the screen, swaps the page at the peak and reveals the new one, in four variants (vortex, wormhole, hyperspace, glitch) that never repeat back to back.

beats.heading: The result: one click, a portal, a new world
beats.claim: Clicking a world card plays a full screen portal tinted to the destination world, swaps the site at the peak and scrolls to the top.

beats.heading: Why the dropdown went
beats.claim: Each of the 17 themes is a full alternate version of the site, so a dropdown hid them; the dropdown was removed from all 17 and every world got world cards.

beats.heading: Cover, swap, reveal: the whole trick in three phases
beats.claim: A state machine runs cover for COVER_MS (720 ms), swaps the world, scrolls to 0 and saves the choice while the screen is fully covered, then reveals for REVEAL_MS (620 ms); those two constants are the knobs.

beats.heading: Why CSS keyframes over canvas
beats.claim: GPU composited transforms and opacity stay smooth over a full screen overlay; JS only picks the variant and times the swap.

beats.heading: Four variants, picked from a shuffle bag
beats.claim: All four variants play once before any repeats, and the bag boundary never repeats the last one, so successive transitions feel distinct (the code comment's own reason).

beats.heading: Reduced motion skips the portal
beats.claim: With prefers-reduced-motion the world swaps instantly with no portal, and a CSS rule hides the overlay as a backstop.

beats.heading: What changed since June
beats.claim: The cards later moved into a picker modal and the reduced motion check became one shared hook; the bag and the three phases are the same at HEAD.
